question: How is bodily discipline (kāyaniyama) to be performed?
premises: The mind is blocked in the heart.
The self's breath is placed in the crown.
The breath is established as yoga concentration.
'In the heart' means absence of attachment to sense objects.
It is not merely abode or station-superintendence of the self.
The breath, self's charioteer, is held by will-power in the self.
It is held in the crown, beyond all principles.
inference: Bodily discipline consists in restraining the senses, fixing the mind in the heart, and raising the breath—self's charioteer—by will-power into the crown beyond all principles as yoga concentration.
uncertainties: The fused compounds (mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ, prāṇamāsthito, viṣṭhāsthānādhiṣṭhānam, icchāśaktyātmani, mūrdhni-sakalatattvātīte) admit multiple syntactic groupings.
The exact referent of 'in the heart' as absence of sense-object attachment versus bodily station is interpretively compressed.
plain_english: Having restrained all the senses, blocked the mind in the heart, and established the breath—self's charioteer—in the crown beyond all principles by will-power, one practices yoga concentration; this is bodily discipline, where 'in the heart' means freedom from attachment to sense objects rather than mere abiding in a bodily station.
